prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin to establish rules for [adoption, redesign], [finish, new_screen], and [sign_in, reorder] since each kind of change has only one test so far.
For [finish, redesign], evidence is mixed across 2 tests: one test won with a +5.1% gain after noise correction, while another showed no clear effect (-1.1% after noise correction).
Predictions were consistently too high for tests that performed poorly and stopped early ([adoption, redesign], [sign_in, reorder], and [finish, new_screen]).
Predictions were too high for [finish, redesign] in round 6, where predicted +5.0% resulted in no clear effect (-1.1% after noise correction).
Predictions were too low for the winning [finish, redesign] test in round 4 (predicted +3.0%, actual +5.1% after noise correction).

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: -7.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: -6.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, redesign: +1.8% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: -7.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 69.7%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 19.2%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [home, new_screen] Desktop Display Readiness Diagnostic Screen: Insert a new diagnostic verification screen during the waiting sequence that verifies overlay display permissions and desktop positioning. (why: 3 support tickets reported pets failing to appear on desktop or app failing to launch. Verifying desktop setup before spawn prevents silent failures.)
1: [finish, new_flow] Desktop Pet Control Practice Flow: Transform the home_intro screen into a interactive spotlight flow where users practice summoning, hiding, and dragging their pet. (why: 3 support tickets reported confusion post-onboarding regarding how to hide or talk to pets, and finish duration is high (395s median).)
2: [home, wait_info] Real-Time Generation Step Breakdown: Display explicit stage milestones with dynamic time estimates while generating the custom pet on the waiting screen. (why: The waiting step has a long median of 201s and mean of 2336s, leading users to believe the app stalled during rendering.)
3: [choose_path, copy] Path Selection Duration Clarification: Clarify path titles and time estimates on choose_path so users understand the fast pre-made path versus custom generation. (why: choose_path drops 23.8% of users and has an 8s median / 514s mean time, indicating hesitation on which path to select.)
4: [home, notification] Background Rendering Readiness System Alert: Enable optional background notifications on the waiting screen so users can safely minimize the app during rendering. (why: High mean wait time (2336s) causes users to close or abandon the app while waiting for pet asset generation.)
5: [adoption, layout] Grid Overview Layout for Pet Choices: Switch the pick_friend screen layout from default to a grid layout displaying pet personality tags. (why: Adoption step has the lowest conversion rate (60.9%). A structured grid reduces scroll friction and speeds up decision-making.)

scores.note: Adding new screens adds onboarding friction; past tests with new_screen performed poorly (-6.4%).
Finish step has high drop-off and strong support evidence, but complex practice flows carry implementation cost.
Real-time breakdown mitigates hesitation during the long wait time (2336s mean) without adding new screens.
Config-only copy change targeting initial step drop-off (23.8%) and hesitation.
Background alerts target long rendering wait times to prevent app exit/abandonment.
Adoption step loses the most users (39.1% drop); grid layout reduces scroll friction, though adoption redesigns need caution.
